conviction_note: SUBC is a merger-arbitrage target pegged at 6.688 Saipem shares plus EUR555m of pre-closing cash dividends. On 2026-11-18 it traded at 307.4 NOK against 292.7 NOK of Saipem stock plus about 19.9 NOK of dividends, so its window move is mostly Saipem's. Saipem publishes Q3 and its first 2027 guidance tonight, and Subsea7 publishes its own Q3 and very likely its first 2027 guide at 08:00 CET. That is two scheduled first guides inside one session, so abs_move is set at 4.5, above the 1.34% median history: Saipem's July guidance cut alone moved SUBC -6.3%. The sell-side previews lean positive but are wire copy, the order-intake read leans negative, and beats on this pegged name have been muted. So p_up is 51 and the scaled number is about +0.1, in line with the +0.2 sum of the findings.

findings.finding: Saipem publishes its Q3 2026 results and first 2027 guidance inside SUBC's window (board 18 Nov, call 19 Nov). SUBC is pegged to 6.688 Saipem shares plus about 19.9 NOK of approved cash dividends: 292.7 NOK of Saipem stock plus dividends against 307.4 NOK spot on 18 Nov, a gross discount of about 1.7%. So about 95% of SUBC's price moves one-for-one with Saipem. Sell-side previews expect a Saipem Q3 EBITDA beat (Barclays EUR447m, +6% vs Bloomberg consensus; BofA +5%) and see the 2027 guide as unaggressive (BofA's own 2027 EBITDA is 10% above consensus but it doubts Saipem will guide there).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Saipem's Q2 2026 release with a 2026 EBITDA guidance cut moved SPM -8.86% and SUBC -6.33% on 2026-07-28, a day Subsea7 published nothing. Saipem's Q3 2025 release: SPM -4.08% on 2025-10-24. SUBC/SPM daily return correlation over 1y is 0.80, beta 0.78 on unaligned closes (Oslo 16:20 vs Milan 17:30).

findings.why_not_priced: The date and the peg are public, but SUBC's own 1.34% median reaction history and its sealed event_move_proxy of 2.28% do not show that a second company's first 2027 guide lands in the same session. The direction is not priced either way: Saipem has fallen from EUR4.65 (12 Oct) to EUR4.11 (18 Nov) into the print despite positive previews. If a beat were fully priced, Saipem would not have de-rated 12% into it. If a disappointment were priced, the previews would not still be calling beats. So the sign is a small lean and the size is large.

findings.finding: Subsea7's Q3 release very likely carries its first 2027 guide, a scheduled first-guide event. Its Q3 2024 release gave 2025 revenue of USD 6.8-7.2bn and its Q3 2025 release gave the first 2026 guide (USD 7.0-7.4bn, about 22% margin). That 2026 guide has since been raised to USD 7.4-7.8bn and about 24%, and 2027 backlog stood at USD 5.6bn at 30 June. Under the 50/50 peg, any surprise moves the combined Saipem7 value by roughly half its standalone size, so this is sized net of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First next-year guide in a Q3 release: +1.04% on 2024-11-21 (2025 guide) and +3.44% on 2025-11-20 (2026 guide). Q1 2026 beat plus guidance raise: +2.52%. Q2 2026 margin-guide raise: +2.62%. Positive on all four guidance events, but every one was muted by the merger peg after Feb 2025.
findings.original_quote: Subsea legger også frem forventninger for neste år. Selskapet venter at omsetningen vil bli på mellom 6,8 og 7,2 milliarder dollar. [Subsea also presents expectations for next year. The company expects revenue of between 6.8 and 7.2 billion dollars.]
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody can price a guide that is not out yet. What is knowable is the habit of a conservative first guide followed by raises (2026 went 7.0-7.4 to 7.4-7.8 and 22% to 24%) and a peer 2027 guide that shows growth. If a strong 2027 guide were already in the price, SUBC would not be -8.0% over 60 days and -4.6% over 5 days into the print.
findings.independence: Peer TechnipFMC 2027 Subsea guide of USD 10.0-10.4bn revenue at a 22.5-24.0% margin (29 Oct 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001681459/000168145926000050/technipfmc2026930-8kerex.htm. Subsea7 Q2 2026 primary release for the 2027 backlog: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=678802

findings.finding: Q3 order intake is likely weak: only three 'sizeable' awards (USD 50-150m each, USD 150-450m in total) were announced in Q3, against USD 2.1bn of intake in Q2 and about USD 2bn of quarterly revenue. Book-to-bill is probably well under 1x and backlog likely fell from USD 13.6bn. Peer TechnipFMC's Q3 Subsea book-to-bill was 0.8x, and it said two or three large awards could slip into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026 book-to-bill of 0.9x (Q1 0.8x) did not stop +2.52% and +2.62% reactions on margin beats. Order-intake misses have not been the deciding line here.
findings.why_not_priced: The awards are public, so a careful analyst has this; a backlog decline headline may still read negatively at 08:00. The Norwegian retail forum already says 'markedet nå har priset inn at ordreboken ikke er hinsides høy' [the market has now priced in that the order book is not extraordinarily high], which is why the size is small. It is an inference: unannounced sub-USD 50m awards and escalations can fill part of the gap.

The findings net to a marginal +0.2, which mildly agrees with a run-up reversal lean but rests on proxies, and the dominant driver (Saipem's guide) is unsigned.
language_note: e24 (Norwegian) documented that Subsea7's Q3 releases carry the next year's first guide ('Subsea legger også frem forventninger for neste år'); the English Q2 release and search snippets did not flag this as a scheduled first-guide event

Nordnet's Norwegian news and forum page carried the dated broker-target sequence (Pareto sell 275 on the morning of 18 Nov, Fearnley upgrade, SEB, SB1, MS, Kepler, Bernstein) and the retail read that low order intake is priced; the English sources carried none of this

The decisive context (the Saipem calendar move to 18 Nov with the 2027 guide, the Equita long-stop analysis, the Barclays and BofA previews) came from Italian sources, not Norwegian ones. NewsWeb filings were in English, as is routine for Nordic issuers
lessons_applied: 'In a live bid, results are noise; the offer is the finding': Subsea7's own-guide finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2 and the order-intake finding from -0.4 to -0.2, because SUBC is pegged to Saipem and its own lines move the combined value by about half. The Saipem-release finding stays the dominant one

'The move is in the guide' (first guides median 9.0%) and 'understatement is the systematic error': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5. Two first 2027 guides land in one session, and the July Saipem cut alone moved SUBC -6.3%
'The reaction history vetoes the direction, not the size': beats on this pegged name have been muted (+1.0% to +3.4%), so p_up pulled from 52 to 51 while abs_move went up
'The bar is unsourced': the quarterly bar is snippet-only, so the print_vs_bar-dependent finding (order intake) stays capped small
